_about: s82-neighbor (Perdón por el ruido): Doña Lupita at her door in the open-air corridor of Departamentos Las Palmas. One set-up, 11 pictures: the introductions, where the learner is from, how they like the place, how things work (the garbage truck's bell), a favor (watering her plants while away), the complaint twist (the party music), the package twist (she took in a parcel), the Sunday cafecito and its time, the goodbye. The other favors (a ladder, some sugar, a package) have no question of their own and keep the 'needs' picture.

items.prompt: Doña Lupita, the neighbor, stands in the open doorway of her apartment about one third from the left, one hand raised in a delighted little wave, meeting the new neighbor from next door with a big, open smile. Potted geraniums beside her door; the sunny courtyard and a palm below the railing.
Change only her pose: Doña Lupita leans forward a little with her head tilted and one hand on her chest, eyes bright with curiosity, asking where the learner is from.
Change only her pose: Doña Lupita sweeps one open hand toward the sunny courtyard and the palm below the railing, beaming proudly, asking how the learner likes the building.

Change only her pose: Doña Lupita cups one hand behind her ear and points down toward the street with the other, eyebrows raised, explaining with a knowing smile that you listen for the garbage truck's bell.
items.note: 5 Nov audit: shown with needs, where she explains the garbage truck's bell; her «¿Necesita algo?» (trash_q) shows needs (the two were one step off).

items.prompt: Change only her pose: Doña Lupita leans against the door frame with her arms loosely folded, a kind, helpful smile, asking whether the learner needs anything.
items.note: 5 Nov audit: shown with trash_q, her «¿Necesita algo? Pregúnteme con confianza».

items.prompt: Change only this: Doña Lupita holds a green plastic watering can by its handle beside the potted geraniums at her door, looking at the learner with an obliging smile and raised eyebrows (when are you leaving?).

Change only this: Doña Lupita wears a quilted floral housecoat over her blouse and stands with her arms crossed, tired eyes and a reproachful frown, one eyebrow raised (the loud music last night kept her awake).
Change only this: Doña Lupita holds out a cardboard parcel with a blank white label toward the learner in both hands, smiling warmly (the delivery man left it with her).

Change only this: Doña Lupita holds a steaming brown clay mug of café de olla in one hand and beckons toward her open door with the other, with an inviting, delighted smile (come over for a cafecito on Sunday).
Change only her pose: Doña Lupita taps her wristwatch (a plain face with no numbers) with one finger, eyebrows raised in a cheerful question (what time suits you?).
Change only her pose: Doña Lupita stands half inside her doorway, one hand on the door, waving goodbye with the other, with a warm, motherly smile.
